The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 345 PM MDT.

* At 153 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Up to 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
mainly rural areas of South Central Otero County

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Globe/Miami, San Carlos, Southeast Gila County and Tonto
Basin.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep monsoon moisture in place across Eastern Arizona will lead
to storms capable of producing rainfall between 1-2 inches per
hours, to locally higher, resulting in an enhanced risk of flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the Northwest Clean Air
Agency until 9 AM PDT Wednesday.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Skagit and Whatcom Counties,
effective immediately through Wednesday July 22nd at 9am due to
expected wildfire smoke from Canadian wildfires.

Particulate matter (PM2.5) levels may reach Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups. When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, sensitive
groups should take steps to reduce exposure. Limit time outside,
avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips for cleaner indoor
air. Everyone should watch for symptoms as a sign to reduce exposure.

For current air quality conditions and additional information visit
https://nwcleanairwa.gov
